_comment: The Tracker (MERGER_PLAN.md 3.5): one file, two lanes. congress stages: Drafted, Introduced, Committee, Floor, Law. agency-court stages: Proposed, Final, In effect, In court, Vacated, State by state. direction: toward competition | away from competition | open. fight: site-neutral | 340b | physician-ownership | research. primary marks the Alliance's own bill for a fight. Every row carries a source URL; the build fails without one. Rojas Media updates a row within two business days of a public action; Dutch signs off on status changes.

rows.issue: Site-neutral payment in statute: Same Care, Lower Cost Act
rows.vehicle: S. 1629, Same Care, Lower Cost Act (119th Congress)
rows.note: Introduced May 6, 2025 and referred to the Senate Committee on Finance. It has not advanced past referral as of November 2026. The bill would apply site-neutral payment to at least 66 service groups from 2027.

rows.issue: Site-neutral payment: Preventing Hospital Overbilling of Medicare Act
rows.note: Introduced April 24, 2025 and referred to the Committees on Energy and Commerce and Ways and Means. It would end the 2015 exceptions and require a unique identifier on commercial claims.

rows.issue: Site-neutral pay: drug administration at off-campus hospital departments
rows.vehicle: CMS, CY 2026 OPPS final rule, CMS-1834-FC, 90 Fed. Reg. 53448
rows.note: Paid at the physician fee schedule equivalent rate from January 1, 2026. CMS estimated $290 million in first-year savings, $70 million of it in beneficiary coinsurance. Rural sole community hospitals exempt.

rows.vehicle: CMS, CY 2027 OPPS final rule, CMS-1850-FC, 91 Fed. Reg. 70284
rows.note: Physician fee schedule equivalent rates at excepted off-campus departments from January 1, 2027. CMS puts the first-year saving at $260 million, $70 million of it in beneficiary coinsurance. Rural sole community hospitals exempt.

rows.issue: Site-neutral: a separate billing identifier for off-campus departments
rows.vehicle: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, Pub. L. 119-75, div. J, title II, § 6225
rows.note: From January 1, 2028, Medicare pays an off-campus hospital outpatient department only for claims billed under its own NPI, separate from the hospital's.

rows.vehicle: H.R. 9504, Tax-Exempt Hospital Transparency Act (119th Congress)
rows.note: Introduced June 29, 2026 and referred to the Committee on Ways and Means. Ordered reported on July 1, 2026 by a vote of 25 to 15. It awaits floor action as of November 2026. The bill requires 340B reporting from tax-exempt hospitals above $100 million in revenue.

rows.vehicle: CMS, CY 2027 OPPS final rule, CMS-1850-FC, 91 Fed. Reg. 70284
rows.note: 340B drugs paid at average sales price minus 28 percent from January 1, 2027, down from plus 6 percent. CMS had proposed minus 33.4 percent.

rows.vehicle: HRSA 340B rebate model pilot; American Hospital Association v. HHS
rows.note: The hospital association sued on October 9, 2026 to stop the revised pilot set to start January 1, 2027.

rows.issue: Repeal Section 6001: Patient Access to Higher Quality Health Care Act
rows.vehicle: H.R. 4002, Patient Access to Higher Quality Health Care Act of 2025 (119th Congress)
rows.note: Introduced June 12, 2025 and referred to the Committees on Energy and Commerce and Ways and Means. It has not advanced past referral as of November 2026. The bill repeals Section 6001 in full.
Medicare closed to new physician-owned hospitals after December 31, 2010; existing ones frozen at their 2010 size. Physician-led competitors stay locked out.

rows.vehicle: CMS hospital price transparency rule, 45 C.F.R. part 180, as amended for 2026
rows.note: Hospitals must post actual allowed amounts; a senior official attests. Research only: the Alliance is not lobbying on this issue.

rows.issue: Medicaid provider taxes and state-directed payments
rows.note: New provider-tax cap began October 1, 2026; payment cuts start 2028. Research only: the Alliance is not lobbying on this issue.

rows.issue: Certificate of need: repeal and reform by state
rows.note: Where repeal and reform stand in every CON state. Research only: the Alliance is not lobbying on this issue.
